277: Discussion. Lipid is localised in the germ and aleurone and carries the fat-soluble vitamins and the aroma compounds. A higher content is preferable, subject to the qualification that excess lipid curtails shelf life. Lipid is stored as triacylglycerol in the germ and aleurone, so that the value reflects both the extent of these tissues in the cultivar and the degree of milling.
278: Earlier reports corroborate this finding. Muchlisyiyah et al. (2023) determined that lipid resides in the germ and aleurone and oxidises readily; Hu et al. (2019) that the movement of water within the kernel displaces the lipid-bearing tissues; Devi and Badwaik (2022) that traditional cultivars differ widely in proximate composition; and Oliveira et al. (2026) that milling is the principal route by which the outer layers are lost. No single cultivar proved superior across all the products: Kalojira, Kalonunia and Tulaipanjii ranked highest in different ones, so that the decision is contingent upon the product concerned.

282: The cultivars separated significantly wherever the attribute was determined. The year effect was non-significant in every product, though the year by cultivar interaction was significant in 1, so that in that product the differences between cultivars were not of equal magnitude in both years. Coefficients of variation ranged from 1.24 to 3.17 %, indicating good experimental precision.
284: Discussion. Ash is the residue remaining after ignition and represents the total inorganic contribution of the grain. Ash follows the germ and aleurone, which carry the greater part of the mineral matter, so that cultivars with a thicker aleurone or a larger embryo return higher values.
285: Comparable results have been published elsewhere. Hu et al. (2019) determined that ash follows the proportion of germ and aleurone surviving; Muchlisyiyah et al. (2023) that the spread in ash derives from the outer grain layers; Jannasch and Wang (2020) that the steeping medium may augment the mineral fraction; and Kumar et al. (2022) that ash is redistributed rather than lost on treatment. The most favourable entry varied between products: Dudeshwar and Lal Badshabhog each ranked highest in one product or another, so that selection is contingent upon the product concerned.

292: Discussion. Phenolic acids are the principal antioxidants of the grain and are largely bound to the pericarp cell wall, so that a higher retained content in the product is preferable. The greater part of the phenolic acid is bound to arabinoxylan in the pericarp wall; heat cleaves these bonds and liberates it while concurrently degrading and leaching the free fraction, so that the value recorded represents the balance of the two processes.
293: Comparable observations appear in the literature. Phimphilai et al. (2026) determined that popping and steam cooking reduce total phenolics markedly; Shavandi et al. (2023) that infrared puffing elevates the extractable fraction; Muchlisyiyah et al. (2023) that heat liberates ferulic and p-coumaric acid from the cell wall; and Kabir et al. (2025) that soaking and cooking reduce phenolic acids, the bound fraction exceeding the free. The leading cultivar varied with the product, Gobindabhog, Radhatilak and Tulaipanjii ranking highest in turn, so that no single recommendation covers the group on this attribute.

299: Discussion. Flavonoids contribute to antioxidant activity and to pericarp colour. They degrade readily on heating, so that the residual content indicates the gentleness of the treatment applied. Flavonoids are synthesised in the pericarp and cultivars differ in the quantity deposited; being readily destroyed by heat, their residual content reflects both the initial level and the treatment.
300: Previous studies describe the same behaviour. Phimphilai et al. (2026) determined that flavonoids degrade more readily than total phenolics; Kabir et al. (2025) that most flavonoid resides in the bound fraction; Oliveira et al. (2026) that protracted cooking may incur losses of up to forty per cent; and Devi and Badwaik (2022) that traditional cultivars differ several fold. The leading position was shared between Gobindabhog and Radhatilak, so that selection on this attribute must be made product by product.

306: Discussion. Antioxidant capacity measures the activity of the entire bioactive fraction rather than its quantity, so that a higher value is desirable. It derives from the surviving phenolics and flavonoids together with the browning products formed during heating, so that cultivars rich in bound phenolics retain more of it.
307: Earlier work is largely concordant. Phimphilai et al. (2026) determined that capacity tracks phenolic and flavonoid content; Shavandi et al. (2023) that activity varies with total phenolics as puffing conditions change; Kabir et al. (2025) that the bound phenolics account for most of the activity; and Muchlisyiyah et al. (2023) that browning products contribute to the measured activity. Kalonunia, Kataribhog and Radhunipagal each headed the ranking in a different product, so that this attribute cannot determine the selection for the group as a whole.

313: Discussion. Phytic acid chelates iron, zinc and calcium in the intestine and precludes their absorption, so that a lower content is preferable, since it liberates the very minerals the grain supplies. Phytate is deposited as globoids in the aleurone during grain filling and is hydrolysed by endogenous phytase during soaking, so that the residue is contingent upon both processes.
314: This is consistent with previous studies. Muchlisyiyah et al. (2023) determined that treated brown rice retains approximately half the phytate of untreated grain; Kumar et al. (2022) that reduced phytate corresponds to greater iron and zinc absorption; Bhar et al. (2022) that the reduction of phytate constitutes a principal nutritional argument for processed grain; and Hu et al. (2019) that germination and hydrothermal treatment operate by different mechanisms. No single cultivar proved superior across all the products: Kalojira, Kalonunia and Tulaipanjii ranked highest in different ones, so that the decision is contingent upon the product concerned.

321: Discussion. Copper is required for iron transport and for several enzymes, cereals constituting a principal dietary source, so that a higher content in the product is preferable. Copper is translocated into the grain by COPT and HMA transporters and sequestered principally in the aleurone, so that cultivars of greater uptake and translocation capacity accumulate more.
322: Published work is concordant. Sonu et al. (2025) determined that genotype governs grain micronutrient concentration; Kumar et al. (2022) that trace metals are redistributed between bran and endosperm rather than lost; Muchlisyiyah et al. (2023) that soluble minerals migrate inward from husk and pericarp; and Hu et al. (2019) that water movement within the kernel displaces elements from the aleurone. The most favourable entry varied between products: Dudeshwar, Kataribhog and Lal Badshabhog each ranked highest in one product or another, so that selection is contingent upon the product concerned.
